prompt: In the relay the lesson describes, product discovers and hands engineering a specification. Where does the lesson say it fails?
hint: When is the collision with the system found?

choices.text: Engineers estimate badly from a written document
choices.why: The estimate takes the blame, but the failure happened earlier, when nobody asked them.

choices.text: The specification is too long for the team to read
choices.why: Length is not the problem; a short specification of the wrong solution fails the same way.

choices.text: The clash with the system shows up mid-build
choices.why: Right: by then the choices are cutting scope in a hurry, unplanned debt, or a missed date.

choices.text: Designers and engineers disagree about the screens
choices.why: Disagreement over screens is a usability question, and the relay's failure is about feasibility.

prompt: Match each of Cagan's four risks to the question it asks.
hint: One of them is about the rest of the business, not the customer.

pairs.right: Will customers choose it, or pay for it?
Can they work out how to use it?
Can we build it with these people, this system and this time?
Does it work for finance, legal, sales and support?

right_distractors: Is it the highest item on the backlog?

prompt: What did Mateus find in the second week of discovery for festival seat maps?
hint: Every seat on a map passes through one module.

choices.text: It needed ADR-0006: maps use the hold path
choices.why: Right: a big festival on-sale on today's hold code would add load to the path the strategy protects first.

choices.text: Organisers did not want reserved areas after all
choices.why: Several organisers asked for it; value looked low-risk from the start.

choices.text: The fee per ticket did not fit areas with different prices
choices.why: That is a viability question, and Otávio's team checked it later and it came back clean.

choices.text: Buyers could not read a map on a phone
choices.why: Usability was tested by the designer with a prototype; it is not what Mateus raised.

prompt: In discovery Mateus said what festival maps depended on and gave no date. Why does the lesson approve?
hint: What does an early number turn into?

choices.text: Dates are product's job alone
choices.why: Engineering does give ranges later; the point is the timing, not the ownership.

choices.text: An early estimate becomes a promise within the week
choices.why: Right: the engineer's job in discovery is the risks, and a date there would be taken as a commitment.

choices.text: The load test had not run yet
choices.why: The load test existed by then; Mateus even used it for a spike.

choices.text: Júlia had asked him to keep schedule out of the discovery calls
choices.why: Nobody asked him for silence; nobody asked him for a date either.

prompt: A product manager proposes that an engineer join discovery once the prototype is approved, to check feasibility. By the lesson, what does that lose?
hint: Engineers bring more than a yes or no.

choices.text: Nothing much, since feasibility is still checked before the build
choices.why: Checked after the solution is chosen, feasibility only vetoes; it no longer shapes the idea.

choices.text: The designer's time, which is spent twice when the prototype changes
choices.why: Rework is a cost, but the lesson's point is what engineers add earlier.

choices.text: The usability test, which needs an engineer to build the prototype
choices.why: A clickable prototype is design's work in the lesson; usability is led by design.

choices.text: Ideas only engineers would offer, and a system-shaped solution
choices.why: Right: engineers know what has become cheap, and Cagan calls them a strong source of new ideas.

prompt: Why does a debt item lose when it is compared with a feature one at a time?
hint: Look at who is in the room for each.

choices.text: Product managers do not understand technical debt
choices.why: The lesson says nobody was unreasonable; the comparison itself is built to tip one way.

choices.text: The feature has a sponsor and a date
choices.why: Right: each deferral looks sensible on its own, and no meeting sees the total interest.

choices.text: Debt items are estimated in hours, which look small
choices.why: Both kinds of work are estimated; the unit is not what tips the comparison.

choices.text: Debt work has no measurable effect
choices.why: Lesson 5 measured it: the seat-hold debt charges about 31 hours a sprint.

prompt: Engineers start hiding refactoring inside feature estimates. What does the lesson say it costs?
hint: What happens to the next honest estimate?

choices.text: The refactoring is done badly, in a hurry
choices.why: Quality of the hidden work is not the lesson's objection; trust in estimates is.

choices.text: Features ship a week late
choices.why: The padding is planned in, so the date holds; the damage shows up later.

choices.text: Product stops trusting any estimate
choices.why: Right: honest estimates then get cut along with the padded ones.

choices.text: Finance flags the overtime
choices.why: No overtime is involved; the work is done inside the estimated time.

prompt: Under Coreto's agreement, which of these go in the engineering share? Choose all that apply.
hint: The bug row was the contested one.

choices.text: Fixing the flaky end-to-end suite
choices.why: Yes: repaying a priced debt is what the share exists for.

choices.text: A bug a venue reported in the Box Office app
choices.why: Coreto put venue bugs on the product side, so the person who talks to venues orders them.

choices.text: Moving a service onto the deploy template
choices.why: Yes: adopting the platform's golden path is investment.

choices.text: Mateus's hours in festival-map discovery
choices.why: Discovery serves a product idea and is counted on the product side.

choices.text: An on-call improvement after an incident
choices.why: Yes: it lowers future interest, so it sits with engineering.

prompt: Coreto keeps one fifth of each sprint for engineering investment. How does the lesson want you to read that fraction?

choices.text: As the industry standard, which is safe to copy
choices.why: Fixed fractions quoted as rules are other companies' decisions for their own debt.

choices.text: As Coreto's choice, sized to its debt
choices.why: Right: a team paying heavy interest needs more, and the share comes down as the interest does.

choices.text: As a minimum, which product cannot borrow from
choices.why: The agreement lets a team lend its share in the on-sale season, repaid the next quarter.

choices.text: As a ceiling on how much engineering work any team may do
choices.why: The Reservations team spends its whole capacity on investment, outside the split.

prompt: Inside Coreto's engineering share, the team's ___ chooses the work and publishes the list at sprint planning.
hint: Not product, and not the CTO.

prompt: Coreto used to keep a product roadmap and a separate technical roadmap. What went wrong?
hint: How many engineers did each plan on?

choices.text: The technical roadmap was too detailed for the board
choices.why: The board never read it; the problem is that nobody read both together.

choices.text: Both counted on the same 52 engineers at once
choices.why: Right: each looked achievable alone, and the conflict surfaced sprint by sprint.

choices.text: Product ignored the technical one on purpose
choices.why: Nothing suggests intent; a document nobody needs to read simply goes unread.

choices.text: The two used different dates for the same releases
choices.why: Dates are not the issue named; the shared people are.

prompt: Box Office staff lose signal at some venue doors. Which roadmap entry is written as a theme, in the lesson's sense?
hint: A theme states the problem and leaves the solution to discovery.

choices.text: An offline cache for the Box Office app
choices.why: That is a feature, one possible answer; it picks the solution before discovery has looked.

choices.text: Box Office app version 4
choices.why: A release name says nothing about which problem it solves.

choices.text: Rewrite the Box Office sync layer in a new framework
choices.why: A solution, and a rewrite at that; the problem it serves is not stated.

choices.text: Doors keep admitting buyers when the network drops
choices.why: Right: it names the problem worth solving and leaves the how open.

prompt: What does the arrow from "Holds without row locks" to "Festival seat maps" tell a reader on the product side?

choices.text: That engineering owns festival maps
choices.why: Festival maps stay a product theme; the arrow shows a dependency, not a transfer.

choices.text: Why that theme waits a column, explained with no engineer present
choices.why: Right: before, that dependency lived in Mateus's head and would have surfaced as a missed date.

choices.text: The date festival maps will ship
choices.why: The roadmap carries no dates; the columns are an order.

choices.text: That the hold work was done for festival maps
choices.why: The hold work serves the strategy's first policy; festival maps happen to need it as well.

prompt: A board member asks Davi when "Load-test gate replaces the freeze", in next, will be done. What answer fits the lesson?
hint: The columns are an order; dates are another course's lesson.

choices.text: The end of next quarter, since next means the quarter after now
choices.why: Next means after something in now finishes, which is an order, not a quarter.

choices.text: A range with a confidence attached, produced the way delivery-metrics lesson 11 shows
choices.why: Right: when a date is needed, the honest form is a range with its confidence.

choices.text: Refuse: the roadmap does not do dates
choices.why: The roadmap has none, but a fair question still gets an honest answer in another form.

choices.text: Ask Júlia, who owns the roadmap
choices.why: The theme is in Davi's lane, and each author answers for their own.

prompt: Júlia wants to push "Move search to the hosted service" to later, to make room in next. By Coreto's rules, what happens?
hint: Who owns the lane, and who agrees to a column move?

choices.text: She moves it; product has the final say on order
choices.why: Each author owns their lane; Júlia does not reorder engineering themes.

choices.text: It goes straight to Helena
choices.why: Escalation is the last rule, for when the two authors cannot agree.

choices.text: It moves if Davi agrees: both lanes change
choices.why: Right: a theme moves between columns when both authors agree, and this one is in Davi's lane.

choices.text: Davi moves a product theme back in return
choices.why: Davi does not reorder product themes either; trading moves is not one of the rules.

prompt: Put the festival seat maps story in the order it happened.
hint: The other three risks were tested while the Reservations team worked.
items: The dependency on ADR-0006 is found
Value, usability and viability are tested
trap: Starting the build before the dependency is found is the relay: the collision then arrives with a date already promised.

prompt: Of Cagan's four risks, the one only engineering can answer is ___.
hint: Can we build it, with these people and this system?

prompt: A startup with a two-year-old codebase copies Coreto's split and keeps one fifth of every sprint for engineering investment. What does the lesson say about that?
hint: What should the size of the share follow?

choices.text: Sensible, since one fifth works for most teams
choices.why: The lesson calls one fifth Coreto's choice and refuses to treat any fraction as a rule.

choices.text: The share should follow the interest its own debt charges, measured before copying
choices.why: Right: the share is sized to the debt, and comes down as the interest does.

choices.text: Too small: a startup moves fast and builds debt quickly
choices.why: Possibly true of some startups, but the lesson asks you to measure the interest, not to assume it.

choices.text: Fine, as long as product approves each item
choices.why: Approval item by item brings back the comparison the split exists to end.

prompt: Why does Coreto count an engineer's discovery time on the product side of the split?
hint: What would happen to the engineering share otherwise?

choices.text: Product pays the engineer's salary during discovery
choices.why: The split divides a team's time, not its payroll.

choices.text: Discovery is not engineering work
choices.why: It is engineering work in the lesson's view; the question is which side's idea it serves.

choices.text: Or debt work shrinks with each idea
choices.why: Right: discovery serves a product idea, so it is counted where product ideas are.

choices.text: Helena decided it to keep the numbers tidy
choices.why: The rule has a reason the lesson states, and tidiness is not it.
